english_translation: I forgot my pencil at home, but my friend helped me.

dialogue.shona: Ndakanganwa penzura yangu kumba asi shamwari yangu yandibatsira.
dialogue.english: I forgot my pencil at home, but my friend helped me.
dialogue.literal_gloss: Ndakanganwa [I (past) nganwa] • penzura [penzura] • yangu [yangu] • kumba [home / to the house] • asi [but / however] • shamwari [friend / friends] • yangu [yangu] • yandibatsira [yandibatsira]

grammar_notes.title: Talking About the Past ('Ndakanganwa')
grammar_notes.content: The verb 'Ndakanganwa' expresses a completed past action. Shona has two main ways to talk about the past: 1) For actions that happened earlier today or very recently, combine the short subject prefix ('nda-' = I, 'wa-' = you, 'a-' = he/she, 'ta-' = we, 'va-' = they) directly with the verb stem (e.g., 'ndamuka' = 'I woke up today', 'wabudirira' = 'you have succeeded'). 2) For events that happened yesterday or further in the past, insert '-ka-' after the subject prefix (e.g., 'takatenga' = 'we bought', 'vakaenda' = 'they went', 'akadanidzira' = 'he shouted').
grammar_notes.rule: Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb

grammar_notes.title: Talking About Location: 'pa-', 'ku-', and 'mu-' ('kumba')
grammar_notes.content:
Look at how location is expressed with 'kumba'. Instead of separate prepositions like 'on', 'to', or 'in', Shona attaches one of three location prefixes directly to the front of a noun:
• 'pa-' means 'at' or 'on' a specific point or surface (e.g., 'patafura' = on the table, 'pamusika' = at the market, 'pasi' = on the ground).
• 'ku-' means 'to', 'from', or 'at' a general destination (e.g., 'kuchikoro' = to school, 'kumusha' = to the rural home, 'kubasa' = at/to work).
• 'mu-' means 'inside' an enclosed space (e.g., 'mumba' = inside the house, 'muguta' = in the city, 'mumugwagwa' = in the road).
grammar_notes.rule: pa- = on / at a point (patafura) | ku- = to / at a place (kuchikoro) | mu- = inside (mumba)

grammar_notes.title: Possessive Pronouns: Saying 'My', 'Your', and 'Our' ('yangu')
grammar_notes.content: In Shona, possessive words like 'yangu' ('my/your/our/their') always follow the noun they belong to! The six core possessive stems are '-ngu' (my), '-ko' (your), '-ke' (his/her/its), '-du' (our), '-nyu' (your plural/polite), and '-vo' (their). A short linking sound ('wa-', 'ya-', 'ra-', 'cha-', 'dza-', 'ma-') attaches to the front of the stem to match the noun: for example, 'shamwari yangu' (my friend), 'munda wako' (your field), 'mabhuku edu' (our books), and 'kubudirira kwenyu' (your success).

cultural_notes.title: Classroom Camaraderie & Sharing Stationery ('Penzura') at School
cultural_notes.content: In Zimbabwean primary and secondary schools, classmates readily share pencils ('penzura'), pens ('zvinyoreso'), and rulers when a friend forgets theirs at home, fostering lifelong school friendships ('ushamwari hwepachikoro').

active_exercises.prompt: Translate this new sentence into English: 'Ndasiya nharembozha yangu pachigaro mumba yokutandarira.'
options: Please close the door and all the windows before sleeping.
I left my mobile phone on the chair in the living room.
My keys are inside the small bag on the table.
We are sitting under the shade tree outside the house.
active_exercises.correct_answer: I left my mobile phone on the chair in the living room.
active_exercises.explanation: 'Ndasiya' = 'I left', 'nharembozha yangu' = 'my mobile phone', 'pachigaro' = 'on the chair', 'mumba yokutandarira' = 'in the living room'.

active_exercises.prompt: Choose the right locative prefix: You want to say 'The keys are ON the table' ('______tafura').
active_exercises.explanation: The prefix 'pa-' means 'on / at a specific surface', so 'pa-' + 'tafura' = 'patafura' ('on the table').

active_exercises.prompt: Translate this new kitchen sentence into English: 'Tichatenga mafuta ekubikisa nemadomasi pamusika.'
options: They cooked sadza and green vegetables for the guests.
Please pour warm milk into the child's cup.
I ate roasted groundnuts and sweet potatoes at home.
We will buy cooking oil and tomatoes at the market.
active_exercises.correct_answer: We will buy cooking oil and tomatoes at the market.
active_exercises.explanation: 'Tichatenga' = 'We will buy', 'mafuta ekubikisa' = 'cooking oil', 'nemadomasi' = 'and tomatoes', 'pamusika' = 'at the market'.
